newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges state firms to use capital markets.
newsitem.headline: China urges state firms to use capital markets.

text.p: The China Securities newspaper on Monday called for state-owned firms to make greater use of capital markets to solve their huge debt problems, rather than simply relying on bank loans and government assistance.

The newspaper quoted Chinese economists as saying state firms' debt problems could not be solved by banks and the government alone and that it was essential for the firms to raise more funds on the capital markets.
The money should come from mutual funds, old-age pension funds, conglomerates and foreign investors, the newspaper said, but gave no details.

Chinese securities authorities have this year allowed dozens of state firms to issue and list shares on the country's two stock markets for the first time, and analysts expect a big increase in corporate bond issues over the next year.
At present, the bulk of the massive debts owed by state firms is held by state banks, placing a significant burden on the banking system.
